sam: Heads-up: noticed Python SDK doesn't export an async throttle middleware that reads quota headers (x-rw-*/X-RateLimit-*) + Retry-After. Any plans? We're re-implementing in multiple services :grimacing:

jia: We have some internal helpers in eng-ml but nothing public. Filing a PR would be fine. What semantics are you expecting for 'quota' and how aggressive should client-side blocking be?

sam: Prefer non-blocking for asyncio. Strategy we want: use Retry-After if present; otherwise consult quota headers (x-rw-quota-remaining / x-rw-quota-reset or X-RateLimit-Remaining + Reset) and apply a token-bucket style limiter with jittered backoff. Should be opt-in middleware, not baked into every request.

anita: +1 on typed helpers. Right now parsing logic is copy/pasted in a couple of places. We should export parse_quota_header and a small QuotaInfo type.

max: Proposed tiny API sketch (pseudo):
```python
class QuotaInfo(NamedTuple):
    limit: int
    remaining: int
    reset_at: float  # unix ts

def parse_quota_header(h: str) -> Optional[QuotaInfo]:
    """Support: x-rw-quota, X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date)."""
    ...
```

rowan: For async runtime, I think middleware should wrap client.send and use an asyncio.Semaphore or a small token-bucket implemented with an async background refill task. Example usage:
```python
client = AsyncClient(...)
client.add_middleware(AsyncThrottleMiddleware(
    window_seconds=60,
    max_tokens=1000,
    policy=ExponentialJitter(base=0.25, cap=5.0)
))
```

dev-bot: deploy-bot: created draft PR #1234: add AsyncThrottleMiddleware + parse_quota_header (WIP)

jia: I'll take a look. Can we ensure middleware is lightweight (no global event loop tasks unless enabled) and exposes hooks for unit tests (e.g., inject a fake time or refill interval)?

sam: Good call. Also need tests for header races: multiple concurrent requests where one sees Retry-After and another doesn't. We had a bug where client-level limiter accepted spikes because header parsing happened after the local token decrement.

anita: :thumbsup: I'll add unit tests for parsing + typing. Exporting a small dataclass/NamedTuple helps mypy users. Also include clear docstring examples for Retry-After variants (seconds vs HTTP-date).

max: One more gotcha: some upstreams send Retry-After as a float string like "0.5" seconds, some send an HTTP-date. parse helper should try int/float parse first then fallback to parsedate.

rowan: Also add a tiny example app in docs showing "how to opt in" and one for "best practice for background tasks that make concurrent requests". That helps onboard people who try to hack it themselves.

sam: SG. @jia can you open a tracking issue and attach the PR link so we don't lose context? I'll move our internal copy into the SDK if we agree on tests and API.

jia: Done — created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/789 and linked PR #1234. I'll ping for reviews when tests land.

sam: Thanks all :rocket:
